topics.topic: Definition and Unicode handling of a character for the 40-character alias limit
questions: What exactly counts as one character for the 40-character limit?
What exactly counts as a character, and is any Unicode normalization performed before the 40-character limit is measured?

judgement.why: This is the same question about alias character counting and Unicode normalization already decided by P1, and the relevant texts have not changed.

precedent.topic: Alias character counting, normalization, preservation, and when length is measured
quotes:
A value that is present is kept exactly as written; Registry trims and
   rewrites nothing (R0-68).

A present value is refused when it is outside the form State 1 declares,
   at stage (4) of A04 rule 6, every such value named: an alias longer than
   40 characters, counted as Unicode code points (R0-90, M01) — its length
   only, its content being the owner's rule (R0-82); an object kind
   outside `apartment`, `house`, `commercial`, `other` (M02); a floor area not
   greater than zero, a number of rooms below 1, or a floor that is not a
   whole number (M02); a customer language outside `es`, `ru`, `en` (M04).
precedent.why: State 2 says aliases are counted as Unicode code points and preserved exactly as submitted, without trimming, rewriting or normalization.

topics.topic: Treatment of empty and whitespace-only aliases
questions: Is an empty or whitespace-only string a present alias, absence of an alias, or an invalid alias?
Is an empty alias, including an empty string or a whitespace-only string, a present alias to display, an invalid alias, or equivalent to having no alias?

judgement.why: This is the same question about absent, empty, and whitespace-only aliases already decided by P2, and the relevant texts have not changed.

precedent.topic: Validity and semantics of empty, whitespace-only, and absent aliases
quotes: An optional value given as an empty string or white space only is absent.

'Correct a project' gives every editable fact of the project: display name,
   alias, customer link and the object — address, kind, characteristics
   (R0-45).

An optional fact the correction does not give is cleared; there is no
   partial correction.
precedent.why: State 2 treats an empty or whitespace-only optional alias as absent, so correcting with it clears the alias rather than storing an empty alias.

topics.topic: Alias canonicalization, storage, and returned representation
questions: Is the alias stored and returned exactly as received, or may Registry trim whitespace, normalize Unicode, fold case, or otherwise canonicalize it before measuring or storing it?

judgement.why: P1 already decides preservation, normalization, and when alias length is measured, which is the same question this topic asks.

topics.topic: Disclosure of aliases containing personal data to the agent
questions: When an alias actually contains a person's name, address or other identifying value, does its field-level `business_confidential` class permit disclosure to the agent, or must the value-level personal-data guarantees prevent disclosure?

quotes:
So an alias whose content breaks the rule does reach the agent, as a room
name that breaks R0-68's rule does. This does not break R0-26: the alias is
held as `business_confidential`, not `personal_data` (State 1, "Disclosure
classes by field"), and Registry's guarantee that no `personal_data` value
reaches an agent covers the values it holds in that class.
judgement.why: The new decision expressly says that an alias remains `business_confidential` despite rule-breaking content and therefore reaches the agent.

topics.topic: Operations that may change aliases and must enforce the length limit
questions: Which operations may set, replace or clear an alias, and on which of them must Registry enforce the limit: project creation, project correction, import, or some other action?

quotes:
A present value is refused when it is outside the form State 1 declares,
   at stage (4) of A04 rule 6, every such value named: an alias longer than
   40 characters, counted as Unicode code points (R0-90, M01) — its length
   only, its content being the owner's rule (R0-82); an object kind
   outside `apartment`, `house`, `commercial`, `other` (M02); a floor area not
   greater than zero, a number of rooms below 1, or a floor that is not a
   whole number (M02); a customer language outside `es`, `ru`, `en` (M04).

The same checks hold
   for every action that gives the value — a create, a correction, and the
   names and aliases the import's mapping gives (A16 rule 1).
judgement.why: State 2 requires the alias-length check for every action supplying an alias and expressly enumerates creation, correction, and import mapping.

topics.topic: Retention of alias snapshots that duplicate Registry-only personal data
questions: May a consumer retain an alias snapshot when the alias's actual content duplicates personal data that R0-80 says only Registry holds?

quotes:
A customer's living personal data — name, contact data, tax id (NIF/NIE/CIF),
legal name — and the object's address and identifying characteristics are held
only by Registry, as the target R0-81 sets for the other services. Other services
keep no customer record and no copy of these values; they read them by
`customer_ref` or project id when they use them.

A project may also carry an alias — a
short neutral label the owner gives it, with no person's name, no address and
nothing else that identifies the object or its customer. The alias is the name
the agent sees in its projection and the one a consumer's kept snapshot holds.
Like room names (R0-68), the alias is a rule on its writer, the owner: Registry
does not inspect it, and an alias that breaks the rule is not refused.

So an alias whose content breaks the rule does reach the agent, as a room
name that breaks R0-68's rule does. This does not break R0-26: the alias is
held as `business_confidential`, not `personal_data` (State 1, "Disclosure
classes by field"), and Registry's guarantee that no `personal_data` value
reaches an agent covers the values it holds in that class.
judgement.divergence: A consumer either retains the rule-breaking alias in its identity snapshot because aliases are snapshot facts classified as `business_confidential`, or omits it because its actual value is a copy of a customer name or object address that other services may not keep; the consumer, owner, and data subject notice the retained copy.
judgement.why: The texts simultaneously require consumers to keep aliases even when Registry accepts identifying content and prohibit other services from keeping copies of customer names and object addresses.

witness.initial: An active project linked to a Customer named Ana García has no alias, and a trusted consumer keeps project identity snapshots.
events: The owner corrects the project and gives it the alias “Ana García”.
The consumer reads the project and updates its kept identity snapshot.
outcomes: The consumer keeps “Ana García” as the alias because a consumer's kept snapshot holds the alias and the rule-breaking alias remains `business_confidential`.
The consumer does not keep “Ana García” because other services keep no copy of the customer's name and read it only when used.
